clue.text: Fingering exercise for string player

parts.note: reads like practice for a violinist, but describes the children's game of looping string round the fingers to make figures

explanation.surface: A practice routine for a cellist's or violinist's fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: The game is played by weaving a loop of string between the fingers into patterns, so it is literally fingering string.

clue.text: Brute left a bird hanging upside down

indicators.note: in a down clue the whole string of pieces is read from bottom to top, as if inverted

parts.note: a mina (also mynah) is an Asian starling that mimics speech

explanation.surface: A brute has left a bird dangling upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hanging upside down' turns the whole run LAMINA backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A brute is a beast, any non-human creature.

clue.text: Indication for traveller to prepare outgoing mail

definitions.meaning: a roadside pointer showing directions to someone on a journey
read as two words: to put one's signature on the letters (the post) before dispatch

explanation.surface: A traveller's pointer, and someone getting letters ready to send.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside pointer tells a journeyer which way to go; split in two it means to sign letters for dispatch.

clue.text: Intended to put the band here?

definitions.text: Intended to put the band here?

parts.words: Intended to put the band here?
parts.note: 'Intended' is a fiancé or fiancée, and the band is the wedding band slipped on during the ceremony

explanation.surface: Seems to ask where someone meant a musical group to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intended' looks like a verb but is the noun for one's betrothed; 'band' is a wedding band, not musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: The wedding band is placed on the third digit of the left hand, the digit named after it.

clue.text: Lift hat to girl in a difficult situation

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting a word raises it so it reads from the bottom up

parts.note: a lid is slang for a hat
Emma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A gentleman raises his hat to a young lady who is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' looks like raising a hat in greeting; it turns LID upwards to give DIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A quandary is an awkward situation with no good way out.

clue.text: Armed boy makes one angry after hold-up

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding a word up turns it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: sore means angry or aggrieved, especially in American usage

explanation.surface: A gun-toting lad gets someone furious following a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold-up' suggests a robbery, but it lifts SORE to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek love god is shown as a winged youth armed with bow and arrows.

clue.text: Salvation that's in the palm of one's hand

definitions.meaning: something thrown to rescue a person, a means of survival

definitions.text: that's in the palm of one's hand
definitions.meaning: palmists read a crease across the palm said to show how long one will live

explanation.surface: Rescue is literally in your own hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope thrown to the drowning saves them; palm readers also name a hand crease this way.

clue.text: Shut up! There's something to be read — verse

parts.note: pent, as in pent-up, means shut in or confined
a meter, such as a gas meter, is something the man comes to read

explanation.surface: Someone told to be quiet because there is reading matter to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up!' looks like a rude command but is the adjective for confined.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of five metrical feet is a standard form of poetry, as in Shakespeare's plays.

clue.text: Gunmen yearn for robbery

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British Army's gunners
to pine is to long or yearn

explanation.surface: Armed men longing to commit a theft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gunmen' suggests robbers, but they are the army's gunners, the Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: Plunder or the forcible seizure of property is an old literary word for theft.

clue.text: Instrument not touched

definitions.meaning: a small box-like harpsichord popular in Tudor England

explanation.surface: A musical instrument nobody has played.
explanation.definitionFit: The early keyboard shares its name with the adjective for pristine or unsullied.

clue.text: People in each group crossing authority

indicators.note: the people are placed within the word for a group

parts.note: a set is a group or collection
men can mean people in general

explanation.surface: People in every team are crossing officialdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' looks like part of the wordplay; with 'authority' it is the definition, a legal right of way.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, this grants a right to cross or use someone else's land.

clue.text: Muse about return of painting

parts.note: c, for circa, means about

indicators.note: a return means the word comes back the other way

parts.note: an oil is a painting in oils

explanation.surface: An artist ponders a canvas being sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muse' looks like a verb meaning ponder; it is one of the nine Greek Muses.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muse of history in Greek myth was one of Zeus's nine daughters.

clue.text: One of the regulars in the services

definitions.text: One of the regulars in the services

parts.words: One of the regulars in the services
parts.note: suggests a professional soldier, but the services are acts of worship and the regular is a faithful attendee

explanation.surface: A career soldier in the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who attends worship every Sunday is a regular at religious services.

clue.text: Recalling phrase from Tennyson's work

definitions.meaning: Latin words used on memorials, meaning in memory of
Tennyson's long elegy for his friend Arthur Hallam

explanation.surface: A quotation borrowed from a Victorian poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin tag for remembrance on tombstones is also the title of Tennyson's elegy of 1850.

clue.text: Clean motor, going all out for this resort?

indicators.note: the letters go flat out in every direction, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Polish the car and race flat out to this Riviera playground.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue nods to the Monte Carlo Rally, where cars go flat out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Monaco district is a famous casino and Riviera holiday destination.

clue.text: Divert attention from London coach?

definitions.meaning: to draw the audience's focus away from another performer
a stagecoach going up to London, since travel to the capital is always 'up'

explanation.surface: Distracting people from a bus to the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Travel towards London is traditionally 'up', so a coach to it is an up stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who moves upstage forces others to turn away from the audience, stealing the scene.

clue.text: Coil one up in strong container

indicators.note: one turned up is placed within the word for the container

parts.note: a solid, sturdy container: solid means strong or robust

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as the word itself, reversed

explanation.surface: Wind a spring up inside a sturdy box.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' means read from the bottom; 'strong container' is a sturdy box, and 'in' says where the turned word goes.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrical coil of wire that becomes a magnet when current flows is this device.

clue.text: Vet gets little creature to swallow pill, though not sick

indicators.note: the creature takes something into its middle, so it goes inside

parts.note: an insect is a small creature

indicators.note: the letters of sick are taken away from the word pill

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: A veterinarian makes a small animal take a tablet although it is healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though not sick' looks like a remark about the animal's health; it is the instruction removing a word for ill from 'pill', leaving one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet something is to examine it carefully, to check it over.

clue.text: Sort of solid, and quite unsexy

definitions.meaning: the five regular polyhedra are named after Plato

explanation.surface: Describing something both firm and entirely without passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato's solids are regular polyhedra; Platonic love is friendship free of desire.

clue.text: Shorten period for ship's berthing

parts.note: to dock is to cut short, as with a tail
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Trimming the time a vessel spends in harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shorten' and 'period' both look nautical-free; DOCK then doubles as the harbour sense in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Charges or space for mooring a vessel in a harbour are this.

clue.text: Shades of meaning?

parts.note: normally subtle nuances, here literally hues that carry information

explanation.surface: Subtle nuances in what words convey.
explanation.definitionFit: A system of hues signalling information, such as wire insulation or resistor bands, gives literal shades that mean something.

clue.text: Jelly-fish?

parts.note: split at the hyphen: a seaweed gel used in labs, and, read as the indefinite article plus a long-snouted pike-like fish, a description of that fish

explanation.surface: Just names the sea creature with stinging tentacles.
explanation.definitionFit: The gel from seaweed used for culturing microbes splits into an article and a pike-like fish.

clue.text: Anchorage found here, an Indian seaman reported

indicators.note: reported means as it is spoken out loud

parts.note: a lascar is a sailor from India or Southeast Asia

explanation.surface: An Indian sailor says a mooring place lies here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anchorage' looks like a mooring, but it is the largest city of the US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Anchorage is the biggest city of the northernmost US state.

clue.text: Greek counts specially to get into this part of Winchester

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the abbreviation
the letters are specially arranged, so they are reworked

explanation.surface: A Greek tallies things carefully to enter this part of an English cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winchester' looks like the Hampshire city, but it is the rifle; 'specially' rearranges 'counts', which goes inside the abbreviation for Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: The wooden butt of a rifle, such as a Winchester repeater, is this part.

clue.text: Scandinavian ruler organised Lapp and Finnish leaders

indicators.note: the leaders of the words are their initial letters, taken in turn

explanation.surface: A Nordic king brought together Lapp and Finnish chiefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' looks like an anagram signal but is just one of the words whose first letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Several kings of Norway and Denmark have borne this name, including the saint.

clue.text: A siren is, oddly, showing such delicacy

indicators.note: the letters behave oddly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A singing sea-nymph shows a light touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Lightness and grace of manner or touch is a form of delicacy.

clue.text: A riddle in game is resolved

indicators.note: resolved means broken down and reformed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzle within a game is solved.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzling thing or mystery, a conundrum, is a riddle.

clue.text: What's under London is a fundamental weakness

definitions.meaning: London stands on clay, so its foundations are literally made of it
a flaw in someone admired, from Nebuchadnezzar's dream in the Book of Daniel

explanation.surface: London's subsoil hides a basic flaw.
explanation.walkthrough: London is built on London Clay, a thick clay bed beneath the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A biblical image of an idol with iron legs and clay base signifies a hidden flaw in someone great.
